38 An -particle passes close to a gold nucleus and is deflected through an angle greater than 90.
Which property of the -particle changes as a result of the deflection?
A
charge
B
momentum
C
nucleon number
D
proton number

hints: Notice the phrase deflected through an angle greater than $90^{\circ}$ - focus on what happens to the direction of motion of the alpha-particle.
Connect direction of velocity to momentum using $p = mv$, remembering that momentum is a vector with magnitude and direction.
Check whether electrostatic repulsion near the gold nucleus can change intrinsic identity such as charge, proton number $2$ or nucleon number $4$ of the alpha-particle.
walkthrough: Identify the event: an alpha-particle with charge $+2e$, proton number $2$ and nucleon number $4$ passes close to a positive gold nucleus and is repelled.
State the governing physics: the force is electrostatic repulsion at a distance, not a nuclear reaction, so the particle keeps its protons, neutrons and charge.
State the vector rule: velocity and momentum are vectors, so a change in direction is a change in the vector even if speed is almost unchanged.
Apply to a deflection greater than $90^{\circ}$: the initial and final velocity directions are very different, so the momentum vector $\vec{p} = m\vec{v}$ must be different after scattering.
Conclude that charge, nucleon number and proton number are unchanged, while the momentum vector changes. This is option B.

A.explanation: Charge stays at $+2e$ because electrostatic deflection by the gold nucleus does not add or remove charge from the alpha-particle.

B.explanation: Momentum $p = mv$ is a vector, so turning through more than $90^{\circ}$ changes its direction and therefore changes momentum.

C.explanation: Nucleon number stays at $4$ because the alpha-particle does not break up or fuse during Rutherford scattering.

D.explanation: Proton number stays at $2$ because no nuclear reaction occurs, only repulsion by the positive gold nucleus.
